decisions.reason: The dietary supplement range is a cheap umbrella option with its own page, and it supports the firm's consumer health expansion, so keeping it open costs little while its value is still uncertain.
The newly launched skin and hair supplement is still early, its prospects are uncertain, and keeping it in pharmacies is inexpensive, so the option is worth holding.
The joint health supplement sits under the established Trivital brand in a steady pharmacy segment, and it costs little to maintain, so there is no evidence yet to justify dropping it.
The mushroom-based immune supplement is a niche product with only a mention on the website, so its prospects are more doubtful, but its low carrying cost argues for waiting for more results.

The 2018 valsartan contamination recall damaged this generic, but re-sourcing the active ingredient lets the firm stay in a large blood pressure market, so the option is kept for now despite substantial risk of withdrawal.
